chunks: 34 - Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:
You will continue to expect (deliverance) and it will continue until Allah sends for this matter one whom you do not know whether he is created or not created.

key_terms.أَمْ لَمْ يُخْلَقْ: Or not created (referring to the concealment of his birth)
key_terms.لِهَذَا الْأَمْرِ: For this matter (referring to the Imamate/Leadership)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by 'whom you do not know whether he is created or not'?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir highlights the perpetual state of *intizar* (expectation) among believers until the emergence of the Mahdi, whose creation was so concealed that people were uncertain if he had been born yet. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the 'Greater Occultation' (al-Ghayba al-Kubra), where the Imam's existence remains hidden from public view to preserve him from enemies, fulfilling the divine promise of inheritance upon the earth.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (34) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali from Muhammad bin Sinan from someone that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:

“You still expect (deliverance) until Allah sends for this matter one, whom you do not know whether he is created or not.” These traditions are clear in referring to the twelfth imam (al-Mahdi) because there has not been any disagreement about the birth of any one of the other eleven imams or about their existence or inexistence besides that none of people has said that any of these eleven imams has disappeared or that seditions have occurred in religion during their periods or confusion has spread among people about the condition of those imams except this imam (al-Qa’im). Imam Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) has declared that when saying: “If three names (of the imams); Muhammad, Ali and al-Hasan succeed, the fourth (imam) will be al-Qa’im.” The will of Allah has determined to make this imam disappear in order to try the people during this disappearance of the authority of Allah and to sift the pure ones, who submit to Allah by believing in His authority even if the authority is not among them and who believe that Allah will never leave the world without an authority even if the person of that authority is absent.
